units.title: Sound Lines: normal timetable, day 9
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update, 06:30. Visibility is good across the Sound and all crossings are operating to the normal timetable, including freight on every sailing. Thank you for your patience during the fog. Expect a lively crossing on the outer route this afternoon in a fresh southwesterly.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, day 9
units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, day 9. Fog cleared overnight. Bright and breezy with sunny spells and a few showers in the west. Wind southwest 4 to 5, occasionally 6 in the outer Sound. Visibility very good. Maximum 10 C. Outlook: changeable, with a deeper area of low pressure possible late next week, details uncertain.

units.title: Tides, day 9
units.author: met
units.text: Tide times, day 9. Port Ammet: low water 00:12 (0.8 m) and 12:25 (0.7 m); high water 06:09 (4.4 m) and 18:37 (4.6 m). Gilliver about 12 minutes later; Lisle about 6 minutes earlier. Big spring tides: wind against tide will raise a steep sea in the Holm channel on the ebb.

units.title: Small craft advice lifted
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard advice. The advice for small craft to remain ashore has been lifted. Wind southwest 4 to 5 with spring tides: expect overfalls off Carrow Point and in the Holm channel on the ebb. Lifejackets on, a means of calling for help, and tell someone ashore your plans.

units.title: Garden waste collections resume
units.author: council
units.text: Waste collection notice. Garden waste collections resume on their normal days this week after the fog. Please make sure bags weigh no more than 20 kg and branches are cut to under one metre. Bags left beside a full bin will not be taken. Thank you.

units.author: power
units.text: Reminder. The planned transformer replacement on Gilliver Back Road goes ahead tomorrow, day 10, from 09:30 to 14:00. Around 60 properties will be without supply. If you rely on electrically powered medical equipment and have not yet spoken to us, please call today.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners: cancellation. The Lisle South cardinal buoy was repaired at 10:40 today and is showing its correct light. The Carrow Point fog signal has been switched off. The earlier notice is cancelled. The survey launch in the Port Ammet approaches completes its work today.

units.title: Fault: Brackwater and east Tollinby
units.author: power
units.text: We are aware of a loss of supply affecting around 1,400 customers in Brackwater, the reservoir cottages and the eastern edge of Tollinby since 19:47. Engineers are on their way to the Brackwater substation. We will update this notice within the hour. Please treat any fallen line as live and keep well away.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines update, 20:15. Ferry services are not affected by the power cut in Brackwater and the Port Ammet terminal is operating normally. Passengers driving to the terminal through the Brackwater junction should allow extra time while the temporary signals are out.

units.title: Evening update, day 9
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update. Clear spells and a fresh southwesterly overnight, minimum 5 C, with a scattering of showers in the west. Tomorrow similar, showers becoming more frequent in the afternoon. Small-craft operators should note wind against tide in the Holm channel around the morning ebb.

units.author: council
units.text: Water supply notice. The final night of Brackwater reservoir outflow valve maintenance, planned for tonight, has been postponed because of the power cut. A new date will be announced. Water supplies are not affected; the pumping station is running on a mobile generator.

units.title: Brackwater junction signals not working
units.author: council
units.text: Roads notice. The temporary signals at the Brackwater junction are not working because of the power cut. Police are attending. Please approach the junction slowly, give way to traffic already in it, and follow any instructions from officers on site.

units.author: power
units.text: Update 22:00. The fault is at Brackwater substation. Engineers are restoring supply in stages by switching from the Tollinby network, and about 600 customers are back on. We expect most remaining customers to be restored by 02:00. A mobile generator is supplying the reservoir pumping station.

units.author: power
units.text: Update 02:30. Supply has been restored to all customers through a temporary arrangement. A damaged component at the substation will be replaced on the morning of day 10; a short planned interruption may be needed and affected customers will be told. Thank you for your patience tonight.

units.title: Live: travel, day 9
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:40. Good morning, and look outside: you can see things. Visibility is excellent across the Sound for the first time in five days and all ferries are on the normal timetable. The Carrow Point fog signal went quiet just before eight last night, and listeners on the headland report the best night's sleep in a week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:45. The Brackwater junction lights are still on their four-minute cycle, so allow time. Otherwise the roads are clear. Watch for low sun on the coast road heading east this morning; it has been a while and some drivers seem to have forgotten what it is like.

units.title: Overnight show: back to normal
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The overnight show returned to more usual business as the fog lifted: a caller from Lisle who had found the drifting rowing boat's lost oar, a nurse on her break asking for a song for her ward, and a long and surprisingly heated debate about whether the Brackwater junction lights had ever, in fact, worked.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:30. Gilliver harbour reports most of the fleet went out before six to lift pots that have been down all week. The fish merchant expects a good market tomorrow, if the crabs have kept their claws, which the fishermen doubt.

units.title: Fog lifts, and Gilliver counts the cost
units.author: courier
units.text: The fog that sat over the Sound for five days cleared overnight, and by six this morning most of Gilliver's boats were heading out to lift pots that had been down since the start of the week.

units.author: courier
units.text: Early catches confirmed the fishermen's fears. Many crabs had lost claws fighting in crowded pots, and one skipper estimated he would get half his usual price. 'It's not a disaster,' he said. 'It's a bad week, and we've had worse ones than this.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said it had carried freight on every crossing today for the first time since the fog arrived, clearing a queue of around forty lorries at Port Ammet by mid-afternoon. The terminal cafe has taken soup off the specials board.

units.title: Timber prices steady despite fog week
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Softwood prices at the Port Ammet timber market held steady this week despite the fog, with buyers apparently content to wait for delayed loads rather than pay more for whatever reached the quay.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Spruce sawlogs fetched within a few cents of last month's average. Pulpwood was slightly weaker, which traders put down to stock the Weyhaven mill built up before the fog arrived, when it feared exactly this kind of week.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Large clearances due to deliver in the coming weeks, including the Kittering Holm job, will add volume to the market, but traders do not expect a significant effect on price. 'It's a lot of trees,' one said, 'but the market has seen a lot of trees before.'

units.title: Dellow Court tenants to write to landlord after meeting
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court met in the block's community room last night and agreed to write formally to the building's managers, Kerrow Estates, about the failing stairwell lights and the lift, which was out of service again this week.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Tenants have compiled a list of dates and times when the lights between the sixth and eighth floors failed. Some residents also described hearing footsteps on the stairs when nobody else was there, which others at the meeting put down to echoes in the concrete stairwell.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A buddy system has been set up so that no resident has to use the stairs alone at night, and the ground-floor shop is selling torches at cost. Kerrow Estates said it would respond to the residents' letter 'in the normal way'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:10. A few showers coming in from the west this afternoon, nothing heavy. Wind southwest, fresh at times on the outer Sound, with a lively sea where the spring tides run against it. Kayakers, maybe tomorrow.

units.title: Lisle buoy light repaired
units.author: courier
units.text: The light on the Lisle South cardinal buoy, which failed during the fog, was repaired this morning by a Lights Board crew working from Lisle pier.

units.author: courier
units.text: The crew found that a seabird had built a nest inside the light's solar panel housing over the summer, and the damp nesting material had eventually shorted a connection. 'We've evicted it and left a note,' an engineer said.

units.title: Port backlog eases as fog clears
units.author: weypost
units.text: The queue of ships off Weyhaven eased today, with seven of the eleven vessels at anchor brought alongside by the afternoon. The port said the extra night shifts would continue until the backlog was cleared.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Hauliers reported shorter waits at the port gate, though the dock road stayed slow at shift change. The port repeated its advice to book collection slots in advance and asked drivers not to wait on the verge by the second roundabout.

units.title: Hauliers catch up after the fog
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Timber hauliers in the Sound began working through a week's backlog today as visibility returned, with some firms running double shifts to move logs from landing stages and roadside stacks.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Operators reminded drivers that hours rules still apply after a quiet week. 'You can't save up hours by sitting in a queue,' one transport manager said. 'Though heaven knows the lads tried.'

units.title: Live: power cut in Brackwater and east Tollinby
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:58. We are getting reports of a power cut across Brackwater and parts of east Tollinby. Sound Power Co-op says around 1,400 customers are affected and engineers are on their way. If you have lost power, please check on neighbours who rely on electrical equipment.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:20. Listeners in Brackwater say there was a loud bang and a blue flash near the substation at about quarter to eight. The co-op has not confirmed the cause. Please stay well away from the substation fence and do not approach any equipment.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:55. The temporary lights at the Brackwater junction are out. Police are directing traffic. A listener says the officer is 'doing a better job than the lights ever did', and would like that passed on to the council.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 21:40. Sound Power says the fault is at the Brackwater substation and supply is being restored in stages from the Tollinby side. The water company says the reservoir pumping station has switched to a mobile generator and water supplies are not affected.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:05. About 600 customers are now back on. The rest of Brackwater village and the reservoir cottages remain off. Brackwater Primary says it will text parents in the morning about opening times.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:00. Messages from the dark: a family in Brackwater playing cards by candlelight, a man on the reservoir road who can hear the generator from his bed, and a Tollinby listener whose freezer is 'ticking ominously'. Keep the freezer shut and it will be fine for many hours.

units.title: Brackwater substation fault cuts power to 1,400
units.author: courier
units.text: A fault at the Brackwater substation cut electricity to around 1,400 homes and businesses in Brackwater and on the eastern edge of Tollinby this evening. Residents living near the site reported a bang and a flash shortly before 20:00.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op said engineers were restoring supply in stages by switching from the Tollinby network, and expected all customers to be reconnected overnight. The co-op said it was too early to give a cause and asked people not to speculate on social media.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Brackwater reservoir pumping station switched to a standby generator, and the water company said supplies were not affected. Police directed traffic at the Brackwater junction after the temporary signals failed. No injuries were reported.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:00. Handing over to the overnight show. The co-op expects most remaining customers to be restored by about 02:00. If your power comes back and then trips, switch off large appliances and turn them back on one at a time.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 02:35. Sound Power says all customers are now back on supply through a temporary arrangement, and a damaged part will be replaced in the morning. Thank you to everyone who sent updates tonight. Now go to bed.

units.title: Your renewal is due in 14 days
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Your Lyle Mutual policy LM-VH-448213 is due for renewal in 14 days. No action is needed if you pay by direct debit; your cover will continue automatically. Peace of mind, renewed! To review your cover or update your details, log in to your account. Terms and conditions apply.

units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Did you know? Lyle Mutual customers can now spread the cost of their renewal over twelve months at no extra charge. It's our way of saying thank you for staying with us. A representative example is available on request. Lyle Mutual: insurance that understands your life.

units.title: Statement schedule notice
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Statement schedule notice. Contract: Kittering Holm. Reference: GLS-KH-0110. Pay statements are issued every seven contract days. Next statement: day 14. Nightly settlement continues as normal. This notice is generated automatically. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Clear skies ahead!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: The fog's gone and the stars are back! Celebrate with 15% off our folding camp chairs, insulated mugs and the cosiest blankets in the Sound. Perfect for a night under the stars, or a night under a roof looking at the stars through the window!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Stargazing tips for beginners! 1. Give your eyes twenty minutes to adjust. 2. Use a red light, not a white one. 3. Find the brightest star and work outwards. 4. A thermos makes everything better. 5. Wrap up warm: it's always colder than you think after dark!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Product spotlight: our Beacon headtorch now has a red night mode, so you can read a map without losing your night vision. Three brightness levels, a rechargeable battery and a strap that doesn't pinch. Only $34, and it fits under a hard hat!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: From the Camp Supply blog: we asked five site managers what they never go without. Answers included a good flask, spare socks, a second lantern and 'a crew who make a decent brew'. What's yours? Read the full article on our website.

units.title: Back, and numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, back from my meeting. The fog's gone, so I'm hoping for a good run over the next few days. Just checking where we are on numbers: no pressure, I'll take whatever the system shows tonight. The boat is back on its normal times from today. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Long-range forecast
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, an early heads-up rather than anything to act on. The Met Office long-range mentions a deeper low arriving toward the end of next week. It may come to nothing. If it doesn't, we'll talk about tying things down and what the boat can and can't do. For now, enjoy the clear spell. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Night rules, a reminder
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the evenings are drawing in, and the insurers have asked again that every site confirms the night rules are being followed. You know where they are in the Journal. I'm not suggesting anything is wrong; it's the same email every site lead gets in week two. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Wages: following up
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, following up on my note from the other day. Payroll still shows crew wages outstanding. I don't want to nag, but this is the kind of thing head office notices, and the crew will notice before they do. If it's a cash-flow problem on site, tell me and we'll see what can be done. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fuel storage
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a short H&S one. Please keep fuel and chain oil away from the camper and the sleeping area, and keep the lids on. A mainland site had a spill this week that ran into a ditch, and it has turned into a very long week for everybody there, including me. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Payslip queries
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a few crews have been replying to the payroll address with questions. Nobody reads it; it's a machine. If anyone on your crew has a query about their pay, they can ring the office or ask you to pass it on, and I'll chase it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Clear evening
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, last one from me today. It's a beautiful clear evening in Port Ammet; I hope you can see the mainland lights from where you are after a week of grey. Have a good night, and please make sure everyone is in before dark. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Clear as a bell
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief, fog's gone. I celebrated by finding all the cones we lost. Forty-one. We had forty. Nobody on the crew can explain the extra cone and nobody wants to take it home. Hal

units.title: lights out at ours
units.author: sam
units.text: power's just gone off here, the whole street, there was a bang somewhere over toward Brackwater. Jamie is doing reading homework by torch and loving it. Pilot is barking at the dark fridge. I'm typing on my phone at 40 percent so this'll be short. love, S x

units.title: Lights out at Brackwater
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Just heard Brackwater's gone dark, substation by the sound of it. I drove past on the way home and saw a blue flash in the mirror. Thought I'd been caught by a speed camera and confessed to my wife before I knew what it was. Hope your lot's on a generator. Hal

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Second thought, from one who has lived in a camper: if your power ever goes, keep the fridge door shut and go to bed early. It's the only thing that works. My old site lead used to say the dark is just the day with the lid on. Anyway. Good night, chief. Hal

units.title: My friend's stairs
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, sorry, it's me again. Nothing important. A friend from work lives in Dellow Court and says the stairwell lights keep going out and people hear footsteps when nobody is there. She laughs about it, but she uses the lift now. I don't know why I'm telling you. Please tell Tomas I'm fine. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: lights back on at ours, so the fish fingers survived. mum rang to check we were all right and then talked for twenty minutes about her hip, which she says is fine really. anyway the dress rehearsal is next week, and Jamie wants to know if you'll be back for the real thing. I said probably not. love, S x

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Also, if Tomas asks, the cat is fine and I have been watering his plant. The plant is not fine. Please don't tell him that part. Is he sleeping? Sorry. Ana

units.title: Is Tomas all right?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, I'm sorry to ask, but I heard someone from the crew went home. Is Tomas all right? Is he still there with you? He hasn't answered his phone, but it never works out there anyway. Please could you tell him to text me when he gets signal. Sorry. Ana

units.title: silly question
units.author: sam
units.text: silly question, but is it dark dark out there at night? like properly? I stood in the garden during the power cut and you could see every star, and I thought, the island must be like that every night. I hope you've got a good lamp. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: PS Pilot has now eaten a sock. not a glove this time, a sock. he's branching out. the vet says he is 'an enthusiast' and charged us for saying so. love, S x

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 2nd. Wind W., fair. Felled 66. Tally 1,402. Men paid to the end of November in coin brought by the boat, every man present & correct. Teague asks to be moved from the north lines to the landing gang. Gave no reason when asked. Mr Dunmore allowed it, being short at the landing in any case.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 5th. Hard frost, still. Felled 52. Very quiet in the woods today, no wind at all, the men remarked on it. Hoskin's hand healed. A fox has been at the pork; set a trap. Lamps to be lit at the hut doors at dusk by Mr Dunmore's order, which uses more oil, but he says it is wanted.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 22 Feb 1904. Middle watch. Wind S 4, clear. 01:00 lamp burning well. 01:45 light of a vessel to the west, distant. 03:10 visibility reduced by a passing shower. Remarks: Doran reports the shore road gate found open at morning; closed it. Probably the carter.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 26 Feb 1904. Middle watch. Wind NW 6, squally. 00:20 glazing streaming. 02:00 engine room checked, fog signal not required. 03:30 relieved. Remarks: wrote to the Board asking for new oilskins for Doran, his being past mending. Weather fit for neither man nor gull.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 18 May 1923. Holm, second day. Searched the gullies above the curing station for deer slots and droppings, for comparison with Lisle. None found in four hours. Hazel unbrowsed, ferns untrodden. Several woodcock flushed. Either the deer are very discreet or they are not here. [Sketch: an unbitten hazel shoot, for the record.]

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mar 14 1934. Fine. Out at 4. Twenty two baskets, the best this year. Ling 5d. Went round by the Holm point on the slack and found our lost buoy in the weed by the old station slip, line still on it. Father said leave it. Took it anyhow. Mother pleased with the catch, not with the buoy.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: Did your mother keep a lamp in the window? EP: Every night. For the boats, she said. Q: Even when your father was home? EP: [pause] Even then. She said it wasn't only our boat. Q: Whose, then? EP: Anybody's, dear. You don't ask your mother things like that. You put the lamp in the window and you go to bed.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The claim that the custom is 'recorded since at least the 1880s' rests on one letter in GV/12 which mentions 'the lamp' without saying what it was for, and a Courier column that may well be describing a shop window. This is poorly sourced. I suggest 'possibly since the 1880s' until something better turns up. Pell.

units.title: Kittering Holm timber camp (1894-95)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: A timber camp operated on Kittering Holm in the winter of 1894-95, felling spruce for pit props and barrel staves. Its clerk, Josiah Penhallow, kept a diary of tallies, wages and weather, transcribed in the Field Notes archive. The camp closed in midwinter, earlier than planned; the reasons are disputed (see talk page).

units.title: From the archive: a buyer for the Holm timber (1896)
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. From the Gilliver correspondence, spring 1896, about a year after the timber camp closed. The 'gentleman from Ammet' has not been identified, and the Courier printed nothing further about him. G. Faulds, archive desk.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: A gentleman from Ammet has been enquiring in the village after boats to carry him to the Holm, with a view to purchasing the timber rights for the coming winter. Your correspondent understands that no Gilliver man would undertake to stay over with him, though several offered to row him across and back by day. The gentleman is said to have returned to Ammet unpersuaded of our hospitality.

units.title: LB-0398: Carrow Point, light mechanism (2001)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0398. Date: 12 January 2001. Location: Carrow Point, beside the old fog signal house. Kit: DAT, M/S pair. Duration: 22:05. Content: wind on the gallery rail, surf, the automated light's rotation mechanism ticking. At 03:14 the recordist's own footsteps on gravel as he moves the stand. Curator's note: included for the mechanism, which was replaced later that year.

units.title: LB-0417: Tollinby caravan field, night ambience (2003)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0417. Date: 9 October 2003. Location: caravan field, Tollinby Common. Kit: minidisc, stereo omni pair. Duration: 58:20. Content: light rain on canvas, tawny owls, distant traffic. A steady low hum throughout, cutting in and out every few minutes, which the recordist identified as the fridge in his own camper van parked 20 m away. Curator's note: he apologises for it in the notes and kept the file anyway.
